extracted.intended_audience: Senior/key personnel and other significant contributors preparing NIH-format biographical sketches for grant applications (e.g., K, R, U awards).
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare an NIH-formatted Biographical Sketch for senior/key personnel or other significant contributors, following the required sections (identifying information; education/training; personal statement; positions and honors; contributions to science; research support) and strict formatting (page limits, field formats).

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the following information for the Senior/key personnel and other significant contributors. Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This instruction applies to each individual Biographical Sketch; the entire sketch for each person must not exceed five pages. Use the exact sections and headings as shown. Treat each person separately (one biosketch per person).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying information (NAME; eRA COMMONS USER NAME; POSITION TITLE)
rubrics_metrics.description: NAME: [full name]  eRA COMMONS USER NAME (credential, e.g., agency login):  POSITION TITLE: [title]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the individual's full name, their eRA Commons user name (or equivalent agency login credential), and a current position title (e.g., Assistant Professor of Medicine). Use the provided fields exactly to identify senior/key personnel and other significant contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: EDUCATION/TRAINING entries
rubrics_metrics.description: EDUCATION/TRAINING (Begin with baccalaureate or other initial professional education, such as nursing, include postdoctoral training and residency training if applicable. Add/delete rows as necessary.)  INSTITUTION AND LOCATION  DEGREE (if applicable)  Completion Date MM/YYYY  FIELD OF STUDY
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List education/training beginning with the baccalaureate and including postdoctoral and residency training where applicable. For each row include institution and location, degree (if applicable), completion date in MM/YYYY format, and field of study. You may add or delete rows as necessary to reflect the individual's training history.

rubrics_metrics.name: A. Personal Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal Statement (narrative about qualifications and relevance to the proposed project).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise personal statement that summarizes the individual's background, expertise, and specific relevance to the proposed project (how their experience/techniques will complement the project). Emphasize past accomplishments and how they will contribute to the submitted application (examples in the document show linking to the PI's K08 proposal and specific technical strengths like imaging and cell biology). Keep the statement focused and relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: B. Positions and Honors
rubrics_metrics.description: Positions (employment history) and Honors (awards, fellowships, distinctions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List positions and employment in chronological order (dates and titles), and list honors/awards (e.g., fellowships, society memberships, prizes). Include relevant fellowships and grant awards that indicate standing in the field. Use clear date ranges and institutional affiliations as shown in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: C. Contribution to Science
rubrics_metrics.description: C. Contribution to Science — narrative descriptions of major scientific contributions with supporting citations (often numbered and followed by representative publications labeled a, b, c, ...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe discrete, significant contributions to science (each contribution as a short narrative) and provide representative publications that document the work (citations may include journal, year, volume/pages, and can include PMCID/PMID). Multiple contributions may be listed (e.g., 1., 2., 3.) with 3–4 representative references per contribution, as in the examples. Include patents, spinouts, or translational impacts when relevant (example: Patent Application WO PCT/GB2009/001111; formation of BliNK Therapeutics Ltd.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative Publications formatting within Contribution to Science
rubrics_metrics.description: Representative publications appear under each Contribution to Science item, often formatted as lettered entries (a), (b), (c), (d) with full citation details and sometimes PMCID/PMID.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a short set of representative peer‑reviewed publications that support each described contribution. Provide enough bibliographic detail to identify the work (authors, year, journal, volume/pages) and include PMCID/PMID when available. Publications lists may be referenced by URL as supplemental (example provided). Do not use this section to list the entire bibliography — select representative works that document the contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: D. Research Support (Current and Completed)
rubrics_metrics.description: D. Research Support — list current and completed research support including grant numbers, project title/description, dates, funding source, and the individual's role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report ongoing and completed research support relevant to the applicant's experience. For each entry include the grant number, PI name (if applicable), project period/dates, funding agency, a one- to two-sentence description of the major goals, and the individual's role (e.g., PI, Co‑Investigator, Biostatistician). Distinguish current/ongoing support from completed support. Provide dates and indicate role clearly as shown in examples.
